gaps.sentence: The rules don't ___ visitors to touch the paintings.
gaps.explanation: allow + object + to-infinitive: allow visitors to touch. (let + bare: let visitors touch.)
avoid is followed by -ing: avoid talking.

gaps.sentence: He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
We stopped at a village ___ some lunch.
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do something: stopped to have lunch.

gaps.sentence: It started ___ just as we left the house.
gaps.explanation: start/begin take either -ing or to-infinitive; with continuous or states, 'to' is preferred. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: I was made ___ the dustbin lorry at six in the morning.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, make takes the to-infinitive: was made to wait.

gaps.sentence: He stopped ___ coffee before bed and now sleeps much better.
gaps.explanation: 'Stop doing' = quit the activity; 'stop to drink' would mean pause in order to drink.
